title: Their affairs by consultation
hook: the believers conduct their affairs by consultation (42:38)

segments.voice: Yesterday, ka-mithlihi, and your line was beyond every picture, still listening. Did the pairs around you, shoes, hands, days, remind you of the One with none? Day five hundred sixty-eight.

Hudaybiya, near Mecca. The Prophet ﷺ has just signed a treaty that some of his companions find hard to accept. He tells them: get up, sacrifice your animals, and shave your heads. There will be no 'umra, no visit to the Kaaba, this year. Nobody moves. He says it three times. Still nobody. He goes into his tent, to his wife Umm Salama, and tells her what's happened. And she gives him advice that changes the afternoon. Bukhari records it. We'll come back to what she said. First, the verse that gives this surah its name.

Surah Ash-Shura, verse thirty-eight, part of a list describing the believers. Pickthall: "And those who answer the call of their Lord and establish worship, and whose affairs are a matter of counsel, and who spend of what We have bestowed on them." Look at the company consultation keeps. Prayer on one side. Giving on the other. Shura, consultation, sits right between them, as part of the description of a believer, not as a management tip. And the surah is counted among those revealed in Mecca, before there was any Muslim state, any government, any council. Consultation was described as a habit of believers before there was anything to govern. Back on day three hundred seventy-three, we heard the Prophet told to consult his companions, even after a consultation went badly. Today, the believers are described as doing it with each other. And now, back to the tent at Hudaybiya. Umm Salama said: Messenger of Allah, do you want them to do it? Then go out, don't say a word to anyone, and sacrifice your animal, and call your barber to shave your head. He did exactly that. And when the companions saw him do it, they got up, sacrificed, and began shaving each other's heads, so eagerly, the report says, that they almost hurt each other. A prophet, receiving revelation, asked his wife what to do, and took her advice. Scholars point to this as a model: consultation isn't a formality, and good counsel can come from the person right beside you.

The practice: decide something together. Sit, and think of one decision coming up, small or large: dinner, a trip, a change at work, how to spend a weekend. Who else does it touch? Picture asking them, really asking, before you've decided. What might they see that you don't? Choose one person, and plan when you'll ask today. Then rest, without carrying the decision alone. The bell holds the time.
Shura, consultation, the practice Ash-Shura names as part of being a believer, alongside prayer and giving. Today's word.
Your line: consult. Today, before you decide one thing that touches someone else, ask them first, and listen to the answer. Day five hundred sixty-eight.

howItsDone: Muslims treat shura, mutual consultation, as a value for families, communities and leadership; scholars have long debated how binding it is on leaders and what forms it should take.

fork.setup: at Hudaybiya, the Prophet has told his companions three times to sacrifice, and no one moves. Umm Salama is in the tent. what does he do?
options: give the order a fourth time.
ask Umm Salama, and take her advice.
fork.reveal: he asked her. she said: go out, say nothing, and sacrifice. he did, and they all followed.

original.note: Arabic: and their affair is consultation among them (42:38).

trapdoor: what you thought: it's good to ask for advice.
what it means: consultation is part of the description of believers, set between prayer and giving.

what a scholar hears: 42:38 is Meccan, so shura precedes any polity; Bukhari 2731–2732 records Umm Salama's counsel at Hudaybiya; jurists debate whether shura is binding (mulzima) or advisory (mu'lima).

sources.quoted: And those who answer the call of their Lord and establish worship, and whose affairs are a matter of counsel, and who spend of what We have bestowed on them.

sources.ref: Sahih al-Bukhari 2731–2732 (Umm Salama's advice at Hudaybiya)

notes: Pickthall wording of 42:38 quoted from memory; please confirm.
Bukhari 2731–2732 cited from memory; the details (three times, shaving each other almost to injury) follow the report; confirm.
Surah 42 as Meccan: standard classification; some verses are sometimes said to be Medinan. Confirm.

Editor review: Hudaybiya was an 'umra, not 'the pilgrimage'; 'between two of the pillars' was wrong (42:38's spending is not limited to zakat); 'many companions think it a humiliation' softened; 'the person you least expect' (about Umm Salama) reworded so it doesn't belittle her; the fork no longer casts the listener as the Prophet.
